"""Approximate the signed response to English indefinite expressions.

After some/any/no, unspecified kinds, ways, amounts and single referents
are negative; collections, descriptive modifiers and comparisons are
positive. Some gives the strongest response. The scope can extend across
one modifier or through 'of'. Ever/anymore have small polarity responses.
These are lexical heuristics, not a full parser; most other tokens are zero.
"""
READS = ()

KINDS = set('kind sort form'.split())
MANNER = set('way reason type'.split())
REFERENCE_POINTS = set('''point extent degree place amount number
    version body day'''.split())
SINGLE_REFERENTS = set('''thing one probability relation method quantity
    factor subset fraction combination portion effect measure stage person
    idea question chance purpose notion possibility circumstance guarantee
    such given arbitrary unknown little value distance part order sense claim
    provision angle event mention matter state difference position cause
    indication intention relationship authority cost size term property object
    guy need power role answer solution problem use exception change tag doubt
    function force case class variable condition rate path issue word'''.split())
COLLECTIONS = set('''examples things comments questions thoughts
    reviews notes'''.split())
ABSTRACT_PLURALS = set('''ways forms types kinds cases instances situations
    circumstances conditions categories species values reasons chances occasions
    contexts embodiments combinations'''.split())
MODIFIERS = set('''important very great basic new good quick interesting extra
    general real key notable preliminary additional necessary relevant old
    possible personal useful helpful significant different serious major
    beautiful hard easy wrong really truly pretty too older deeper specific
    short'''.split())
MASS = set('money research help information data news homework'.split())
TIME_UNITS = set('''seconds minutes hours days weeks months years
    decades centuries moments times'''.split())
DESCRIPTIVE = MODIFIERS | MASS
COMPARATIVES = set('more less further longer better worse harder easier'.split())
SCALES = {'some': 1.0, 'any': 0.56, 'no': 0.50,
          'few': 0.52, 'many': 0.20, 'several': 0.15,
          'certain': 0.27, 'little': 0.40, 'bit': 0.32,
          'nothing': 0.40, 'something': 0.27, 'anything': 0.32}
NEGATIVE_NOUNS = KINDS | MANNER | REFERENCE_POINTS | SINGLE_REFERENTS


def response(word):
    for group, value in (
        (KINDS, -4.05),
        (MANNER, -3.3),
        (REFERENCE_POINTS, -2.6),
        (SINGLE_REFERENTS, -1.4),
        (COLLECTIONS, 2.35),
        (TIME_UNITS, 1.35),
        (ABSTRACT_PLURALS, 0.15),
        (DESCRIPTIVE, 1.15),
    ):
        if word in group:
            return value
    if word in {'people', 'ideas'}:
        return 1.65
    if word == 'means' or word.startswith('sembl'):
        return -1.6
    if word == 'time':
        return -0.55
    if word.isascii() and word.isalpha() and len(word) > 3:
        if word.endswith('s') and not word.endswith(('ss', 'ous', 'us', 'is')):
            return 0.8
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev, before = ('', '') if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1:]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    scale = SCALES.get(prev, 0.0)
    value = scale * response(word) if scale else 0.0
    if scale:
        if word in COMPARATIVES:
            value = scale * (3.6 if word == 'more' else 2.6)
            if word == 'more' and prev in {'any', 'no'}:
                value = 2.56 if prev == 'any' else 2.3
            elif word == 'longer' and prev == 'no':
                value = 0.67
        elif word == 'of':
            value = {'some': 1.75, 'any': -0.17, 'no': -0.10,
                     'many': 0.32, 'few': 0.43}.get(prev, 0.4)
        elif word == 'other':
            value = {'some': -1.7, 'any': -0.42, 'no': -0.47}.get(prev, 0.0)
    elif before in SCALES and (prev in MODIFIERS or prev == 'other'):
        value = 0.4 * SCALES[before] * response(word)
    if word == 'of':
        if prev in NEGATIVE_NOUNS and before in SCALES:
            weight = 1.02 if prev in {'kind', 'sort'} else 0.75
            value = weight * SCALES[before] * response(prev)
        elif prev in KINDS | {'type', 'number'}:
            value = -0.5 if before in {'a', 'the', 'what'} else -0.12
        if not token[:1].isspace():
            value *= 0.25
    if scale and token.isupper():
        value *= 0.60
    elif scale and not token[:1].isspace() and token[:1].isupper():
        value *= 0.75
    if word == 'some' and not prev:
        value = 1.8 if token[:1].isspace() else 1.55
    if word == 'anymore':
        value = 0.95
    elif word == 'ever':
        value = -0.33

"""Layer-0 MLP component down_proj:5235 of Qwen3-1.7B: a sparse, mostly negative feature.

Almost everywhere it sits near zero. Its strong responses are to Japanese and Chinese
tokens where a grammatical word has been fused onto the front of a token:

- Case particles and copulas opening a multi-character token (を, に, が, 为, 的, 是) dip
  to about -1.2. Other particles, copulas and adverbs (で, の, と, は, も, 了, 也, 就, 都,
  有, 还, 在, 会, 要 ...) dip weakly, to about -0.3.
- When such a token also ends in 不 or 一 (的一, 就不, 也不, 有一, 是最) the dip is much
  deeper, about -4.7 for the particle openers and -3.8 for the weaker ones.
- Honorific お fused onto a particle (にお, をお) dips hardest, to about -5.
- Polite Japanese endings (です, ます, ました, ...) dip to about -1.3.
- Arabic tokens that open with the article ال or a clitic (ل, و, ب, أ, إ) dip to about
  -0.5; other Arabic tokens to about -0.1.
- The end-of-thinking tag </think> is the one clear positive, about +1.1.

Everything else is 0. The program reads only the newest token, so it needs no carry, and
it does not look at the rest of the context.
"""

READS = ()

# Particles and copulas that open a token with the strongest dips.
STRONG_OPENERS = set("をにが为的是")
# Other grammatical words (particles, copula, aspect, adverbs) that open a weaker dip.
FUNCTION_OPENERS = set("をにがでのとはもへやからまで为的是了也就都有还在而如以会可要将")
POLITE_ENDINGS = ("です", "ます", "ました", "ません", "ください", "します", "います",
                  "おります", "でしょう", "ましょう", "でした")
ARABIC_PREFIXES = ("ال", "ل", "و", "ب", "أ", "إ")


def _cjk(ch):
    code = ord(ch)
    return 0x3040 <= code <= 0x30FF or 0x4E00 <= code <= 0x9FFF or 0x3400 <= code <= 0x4DBF


def _arabic(ch):
    return "؀" <= ch <= "ۿ"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    value = 0.0
    if token == "</think>":
        value = 1.1
    elif token.endswith(POLITE_ENDINGS):
        value = -1.3
    elif len(token) >= 2 and all(_cjk(ch) for ch in token):
        if token[0] in STRONG_OPENERS:
            value = -1.2
        elif token[0] in FUNCTION_OPENERS:
            value = -0.3
        if token[0] in FUNCTION_OPENERS and token[-1] in "不一":
            value -= 3.5
        if token[0] in "をに" and token[1:].startswith("お"):
            value = -5.0
    elif any(_arabic(ch) for ch in token):
        value = -0.5 if token.startswith(ARABIC_PREFIXES) else -0.1

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:5236: a "closing a block of code" detector.

Mostly silent (near 0). It goes strongly negative on tokens that CLOSE a block of code:

1. The closing Markdown code fence. The tokenizer splits it as "\\n", "``", "`\\n\\n":
   the "``" right after a line of code (it ends in ; ) } > ] or is a newline) is about -2,
   and the "`\\n\\n" or "`\\n" that follows it is about -3. An inline "``" after prose is ~0.
2. A closing brace "}" that starts a line or follows indentation: about -0.7. A brace
   after a letter or digit (e.g. "x}", "\\frac{1}{2}") is ~0.
3. A "return" or "end" statement, and "*/": about -0.4 (the last line before a closing brace).
4. The first prose word right after a closed fence: about -0.5.
5. A small positive push on " if" (about +0.15).

The numbers are rough magnitudes read off the activation data, not fitted parameters.
Variance explained is only about 0.15 on eval rows (about 0.24 on a local training sample),
because the component is sparse: a few large negative spikes carry most of its variance.
"""

READS = ()

CODE_END_CHARS = (";", ")", "}", ">", "]")
BRACE = {"}", "}\n", "}\n\n", "}\r\n", "});", "});\n", " }", " }\n", " }\n\n", " });\n", " });"}
RETURN_LIKE = {" return", "\treturn", "return", "end", "*/\n", "*/"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    # The previous token ends a line of code, or is a line break or indentation.
    after_code_line = prev.endswith("\n") or prev.endswith(CODE_END_CHARS) or prev.strip() == ""
    line_start = prev.endswith("\n") or prev.endswith("\t") or prev.strip() == ""
    just_closed_fence = carry == "closed"

    if tok in ("`\n\n", "`\n") and prev in ("``", "```"):
        return "closed", -3.0  # closing fence, second half
    if tok == "``" and after_code_line:
        return None, -2.0  # closing fence, first half
    if tok == "```" and after_code_line:
        return None, -1.0
    if tok in BRACE and line_start:
        return None, -0.7  # closing brace of a block
    if tok in RETURN_LIKE:
        return None, -0.4
    if just_closed_fence:
        return None, -0.5  # first prose token after a closed code block
    if tok == " if":
        return None, 0.15
    return None, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""Approximate a boundary signal for informative, explanatory prose.

Sentence-ending line breaks grow with line length and with words about
assistance, resources and importance; paragraph breaks are stronger. Digits
and capitals dampen this response. Within informative lines, ordinary words
get a small negative continuation signal. Named word classes, headings,
closing delimiters and chat markers add weaker surface-form biases.

This deliberately leaves most idiosyncratic lexical responses unexplained.
The state stores only the current document, line, chat role and style count.
"""
import re

READS = ()
GUIDANCE = set("""
practices guidelines strategies measures planning decisions feedback advice guidance
""".split())
RESOURCES = set("information management development resources material".split())
IMPORTANCE = set("""
potential relevant valuable informed responsible important efficient effective
reliable comprehensive sensitive practical
""".split())
ASSISTANCE = set("""
enhance ensure provide protect encourage promote contribute develop maintain
prevent reduce allow achieve manage
""".split())


def verb_forms(bases):
    forms = set(bases)
    for word in bases:
        stem = word[:-1] if word.endswith("e") else word
        forms.update((word + "s", stem + "ing", stem + "ed"))
    return forms


EXPLANATORY = verb_forms(ASSISTANCE | set("""
help improve support increase enable facilitate create benefit understand
""".split()))
ABSTRACT = GUIDANCE | RESOURCES | IMPORTANCE | set("""
quality knowledge experience safety security opportunities challenges growth
performance efficiency reliability learning skills systems understanding
""".split())
COMPARISONS = set("more further better".split())
REFERENCES = set("own each our its it these".split())
EXAMPLES = set("including such".split())
NEEDS = set("need needs".split())
NEWNESS = set("new fresh real".split())
INFERENCE_STARTERS = set("As Since Therefore Thus Now Also From".split())
INTRODUCERS = set("It Here One However While".split())


def word_bias(token):
    word = token.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    if token.startswith(" "):
        if word in INTRODUCERS:
            return 0.077
        for group, weight in ((GUIDANCE, -0.105), (ASSISTANCE, -0.043)):
            if lower in group:
                return weight
        if word.islower():
            if lower in RESOURCES:
                return -0.062
            if lower in IMPORTANCE:
                return -0.065
        for group, weight in ((COMPARISONS, -0.039), (REFERENCES, -0.036),
                              (EXAMPLES, -0.036), (NEEDS, -0.038),
                              (NEWNESS, 0.055)):
            if lower in group:
                return weight
        if lower == "must":
            return 0.047
    if word in INFERENCE_STARTERS:
        return -0.06
    if word in {"That", "These"}:
        return -0.08
    if token == "The":
        return -0.046
    if token and set(token) == {"#"}:
        return 0.125 if len(token) >= 3 else 0.015 * len(token)
    if token == "<think>":
        return -0.082
    if token == "<|im_end|>":
        return 0.036
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    line, role, style = (("", "", 0) if carry is None or carry[0] != doc
                         else carry[1:])
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if token == "<|im_start|>":
        role = "header"
    elif role == "header" and word in {"user", "assistant", "system"}:
        role = word
    elif token == "<think>":
        role = "think"
    elif token == "</think>":
        role = "assistant"
    value = word_bias(token)
    if "\n" not in token:
        style += word in EXPLANATORY or word in ABSTRACT
        if token.startswith(" ") and word.isalpha() and token.strip().islower():
            value -= 0.005 * min(style, 8)
        line = (line + token)[-1800:]
        return (doc, line, role, style), float(value)

    end = token.split("\n", 1)[0]
    text = line + end
    n = max(len(text), 1)
    blank = token.count("\n") >= 2
    punctuation = end.strip().strip('\"”\'’)]')
    sentence = punctuation in {".", "!", "?", "。"}
    spaced = end.isspace() and len(end) <= 3
    if sentence or spaced:
        if punctuation == "。":
            value = (0.24 + 0.24 * min(n, 150) / 150 if blank
                     else -0.015 + 0.12 * min(n, 100) / 100)
        else:
            words = re.findall(r"[a-z]+", text.lower())
            count = lambda group: min(sum(w in group for w in words), 12)
            value = ((0.0 if blank else -0.065)
                     + (0.085 if blank else 0.057) * min(n, 100) / 100
                     + (0.12 if blank else 0.045)
                     * min(max(n - 100, 0), 200) / 200
                     + (0.055 if blank else 0.037) * count(EXPLANATORY)
                     + 0.025 * count(ABSTRACT)
                     + (0.10 if blank else 0.05) * (role == "assistant")
                     + (0.085 if blank else 0.04)
                     * bool(re.match(r"^\s*(?:#|[-*]|[0-9]+\.)", text)))
            if spaced:
                value *= 0.65 if blank else 0.15
                if len(end) == 2:
                    value += 0.09
            elif punctuation == "?":
                value = value * 0.7 - 0.015
            elif len(end) > 1:
                value *= 0.8
        value -= (0.16 * sum(c.isdigit() for c in text)
                  + 0.17 * sum(c.isupper() for c in text)
                  + 0.10 * sum(c in '$=\\_{}[]<>|/' for c in text)) / n
        value = max(-0.15, min(value, 0.65))
    elif blank and end.rstrip().endswith(("}", ")", "]", ">", "`")):
        value = 0.08 if end.startswith(" ") or end.endswith((">", "`")) else 0.045
    elif not end:
        value = 0.025 if blank and role else (-0.012 if blank else 0.006)
    else:
        value = 0.0
    line = token.rsplit("\n", 1)[-1]
    return (doc, line, role, 0), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:5237 as a paragraph-end detector.

What the component does, in plain terms: it fires on the token that closes a paragraph or
line of prose, a sentence-final mark (. 。 ! ? or a closing quote or bracket) followed by a
newline, as in ".\\n\\n". It fires harder the longer the paragraph was, rising over the first
~45 words of the line and then flat. Almost every other token gives roughly zero.

The program: at each token, if the token is a paragraph or line break after a sentence end,
predict a weight for that kind of break times how many words the line has run so far (capped
at 45). Anything else predicts 0. The count of words resets at every newline and at every
document boundary.

What it leaves out: the component has a long tail of small token-specific offsets (for
example "The", " it", " own" are negative; " It", "###", " However" are positive) that no
short rule captures. A 1000-token lookup table reaches about R^2 0.14 on held-out text;
this rule reaches about 0.04.
"""

READS = ()

LINE_CAP = 45  # words after which a line's length stops adding to the activation

# Weight of a break, by what precedes its newline.
CJK_STOP = 0.5        # 。 then newline(s): the Chinese full stop
SENTENCE_END = 0.18   # . ! ? (or ." .” ) then a blank line
SENTENCE_LINE = 0.04  # the same mark then a single newline
BARE_BREAK = 0.1      # a newline after only spaces, e.g. "  \n" or " \n\n"
CLOSING = 0.1         # a closing bracket or colon before a blank line, e.g. ")\n\n"

SENTENCE_MARKS = (".", "!", "?", '."', ".”", '?"', '!"')


def break_weight(token):
    """How strongly a token is a paragraph or line break, from 0 to a few tenths."""
    if "\n" not in token:
        return 0.0
    body = token[: token.index("\n")]
    blank_line = token.count("\n") >= 2
    if body.strip() == "":
        return BARE_BREAK if blank_line else 0.0
    if body.endswith("。"):
        return CJK_STOP if blank_line else SENTENCE_LINE
    if body.endswith(SENTENCE_MARKS):
        return SENTENCE_END if blank_line else SENTENCE_LINE
    if body.endswith((")", "}", ":")) and blank_line:
        return CLOSING
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict the component's activation at the newest token.

    carry is (document id, words so far on this line), or None at a row's start.
    """
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        words = 0
    else:
        words = carry[1]
    value = break_weight(token) * min(words, LINE_CAP) / LINE_CAP
    if "\n" in token:
        words = 0
    elif token.strip():
        words += 1
    return (doc, words), float(value)

"""Component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:5239 — a "without" detector.

What it does: the component goes strongly negative on the word "without" (about -9.4
on " without", and about the same on " WITHOUT" / "Without"). It is moderately negative
(about -5) on the same word in other languages: " sans" (French), " ohne" (German),
" senza" (Italian), " без" (Russian), " zonder" (Dutch). It is weakly negative
(about -0.5 to -1.5) on prepositions that tie a phrase to a condition, a company or a
time: " with", " before", " after", " despite", " unless", " except", " within",
" outside", " against", " regardless", and on " than" right after " rather".
Everywhere else it is near zero. The sign is the component's own: it is negative on
these words.

The program needs no memory of earlier tokens: it reads only the newest token.
"""

READS = ()

# The word "without", in English spelling variants.
WITHOUT = {" without", " Without", " WITHOUT", "without", "Without", "_without"}

# "Without" in other languages (French, German, Italian, Russian, Dutch, Portuguese).
FOREIGN_WITHOUT = {" sans", " Sans", "sans", " ohne", " senza", " без", " zonder", " sem", " bez", " utan", " uten"}

# " with" on its own is about -0.5; the rest of this set is about -1.
WITH_WORD = {" with", "With", " With", "with"}
CONTRAST_PREPOSITIONS = {
    " before", " Before", "Before", " after", " After", "After", " unless", " Unless",
    " except", " Except", " despite", " Despite", " beyond", " Beyond", " within", " outside",
    " inside", " against", " plus", " besides", " regardless", " avoid", " avoiding",
    " absence", " absent", " lacking", " lack", " WITH",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if token in WITHOUT:
        value = -9.4
    elif token in FOREIGN_WITHOUT:
        value = -4.0
    elif token == " with":
        value = -0.5
    elif token in WITH_WORD or token in CONTRAST_PREPOSITIONS:
        value = -1.0
    elif token == " than" and previous == " rather":
        value = -1.5
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

    "及时", "依法", "全面", "全部", "共同", "迅速", "有效", "积极", "切实", "不断",
    "相互", "互相", "再次", "正式", "长期", "大力", "尽快", "直接", "突然", "快速",

    "广泛", "尽量", "严格", "从而", "常常", "然后", "仍然",
}

WEAK_VALUE = 0.0
SCOPE_VALUE = -0.15

    """A whole English word (leading space), ending -ly, not in the weak list."""
    if not token.startswith(" "):

    word = token[1:]
    if word in EN_MANNER:

    return word.isalpha() and word.endswith("ly") and not word.endswith("ally") and len(word) > 4

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    bare = token.strip()
    if bare in ZH_MANNER:

    if bare in ZH_SCOPE:
        return carry, SCOPE_VALUE
    if token.startswith(" ") and bare in EN_WEAK:
        return carry, WEAK_VALUE
    if _english_manner(token):
        return carry, MANNER_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

    "全都", "全て",
    "安心", "安全", "日々", "进行", "まで", "бесплатный",
})


def _last_word(text):
    end = len(text)
    start = end
    while start and unicodedata.category(text[start - 1])[0] in "LM":
        start -= 1
    return text[start:end]

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry and carry[0] == document else ""
    fragment = token.lstrip() if token[:1].isspace() else previous + token
    word = _last_word(fragment)
    next_carry = (document, word[-40:])

    word = word.casefold()
    is_adverb_shaped = len(word) >= 6 and word.endswith("ly")
    value = 0.115 if is_adverb_shaped or word in MODIFIERS else 0.0
    return next_carry, value

"""Local Chinese modifier--predicate pulses, not a full activation model.

Look for a Han-character token after a token ending in a listed Chinese
modifier. Predicate stems get larger negative pulses; degree modifiers
before 显/顯 (appear) are especially strong. Multi-character tokens weaken
these pulses. Negation 不/无/無 has a positive baseline, increased after
emphatic degree words or the modifying particle 的. Other token-specific
background variation is omitted. Remember only the preceding token, and
reset it at document boundaries.
"""
READS = ()

LITERARY_MODIFIERS = set(
    '再又'          # again / also
    '仅僅兼'        # only / both
    '初未既犹猶'    # initially / not yet / already / still
    '所'            # nominalized predicate
)
DEGREE_MODIFIERS = set('更略稍颇頗倍甚深极極愈')
OTHER_MODIFIERS = set(
    '复復已尚仍先曾久乍早'    # aspect and time
    '而且并並亦皆共遂'        # coordination and continuation
    '不無无莫勿若可应應宜须須必欲只毋自独獨'  # modality and negation
)
PREDICATE_STEMS = set(
    '显顯趋趨呈现現露'                    # appearance
    '见見闻聞睹识識知懂觉覺观觀听聽看读讀'  # perception
    '思虑慮念想悟忆憶记記'                # thought
    '作做起立成生兴興建造创創'            # creation / emergence
    '收获獲得存剩限有持取付授予'          # possession / acquisition
    '上开開接添增减減加去来來行走进進至到入出落下续續藏'
    '当當兼为為喜悅悦'                    # roles and states
)
EMPHATIC_DEGREE_WORDS = {'极其', '極其', '极度', '極度', '非常', '十分'}
NEGATION = {'不', '无', '無'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    current = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    value = 0.0
    if current in NEGATION:
        value = .15
        if previous.strip() in EMPHATIC_DEGREE_WORDS:
            value = .55
        elif previous.endswith('的'):
            value = .4

    previous = previous.strip()
    if previous and current and all('\u3400' <= c <= '\u9fff' for c in current):
        modifier = previous[-1]
        strength = (1.0 if modifier in LITERARY_MODIFIERS else
                    .65 if modifier in DEGREE_MODIFIERS else
                    .45 if modifier in OTHER_MODIFIERS else 0.0)
        pulse = .70 if current[0] in PREDICATE_STEMS else .32
        pulse *= strength
        if current[0] in '显顯' and modifier in DEGREE_MODIFIERS:
            pulse = 1.15
        pulse *= 1.0 if len(current) == 1 else .35
        pulse *= 1.0 if len(previous) == 1 else .55
        value -= pulse

    return (doc, current), value

"""Layer-0 MLP component 5243 (down_proj), a dip on the character after an adverb.

Its activation is mostly small and has no simple pattern, but on a Chinese character that
directly follows certain adverbs or function words it is clearly negative. Those words
(更 more, 再 again, 又 again/also, 仅 only, 略 slightly, 颇 rather, 稍 a little, 既 already,
兼 and also, 犹 still, 而 and, 所 (passive "that which"), 初 at first, 未 not yet) all
introduce a verb or adjective, as in 更|显 (more visible), 再|起 (rise again), 仅|限
(limited to), 略|显 (slightly visible). The program predicts a negative value there, about
the average size seen in the data, and 0 everywhere else.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical activation on the character after each word (negative = dip).
ADVERB_DIP = {
    "更": -0.35, "再": -0.27, "又": -0.22, "仅": -0.3, "略": -0.3, "颇": -0.3,
    "稍": -0.3, "既": -0.3, "兼": -0.3, "犹": -0.3, "而": -0.14, "所": -0.2,
    "初": -0.3, "未": -0.2,
}


def is_chinese_char(text: str) -> bool:
    return len(text) == 1 and "一" <= text <= "鿿"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    words = prefix.token_strings
    same_doc = len(words) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] == prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if same_doc and is_chinese_char(words[-1]):
        return carry, float(ADVERB_DIP.get(words[-2], 0.0))
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:5245: the letter "i" at the start of a word.

This component reads the current token, and for word starts the token before it.
It fires when the token is a word or identifier that begins with the letter I or i,
and is near zero otherwise:

* capital-I words ("I", "It", "If", "Id", "IC", "IP", "Iran", "International")
  fire harder than lowercase ones ("it", "if", "id", "im", "ignore");
* a word start fires harder than a fragment glued onto the piece before it. A word
  starts after a space, after a separator such as "_", ".", "-", "/", "(", after a
  newline or other punctuation, or at the first token of a document;
* short words (one or two letters: "I", "it", "id") fire harder than longer ones;
* the common function words "in", "is", "its", "into", "instead" and the "include"
  family do not fire, nor does any other token;
* the i-sound letter in other scripts fires about as strongly as a Latin I: a
  Cyrillic и or і starting a word (" и", " і"), and the Japanese syllables イ and い.

Everything else predicts 0.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# optional separators (spaces and punctuation), then a run of Latin letters
WORD = re.compile(r"^([\s_.\-/(\[\"<'“]*)([A-Za-z]+)")
STOP = {
    "in", "is", "its", "into", "instead", "inside",
    "include", "includes", "included", "including",
}
OTHER_SCRIPT_I = ("イ", "い")
OTHER_SCRIPT_WORD_START = (" и", " И", " і")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok in OTHER_SCRIPT_I or tok.startswith(OTHER_SCRIPT_WORD_START):
        return carry, 0.9
    m = WORD.match(tok)
    if m is None or m.group(2)[0] not in "Ii":
        return carry, 0.0
    word = m.group(2)
    if word.lower() in STOP:
        return carry, 0.0
    value = 1.5 if word[0] == "I" else 0.9      # capital I words are stronger
    if prefix.position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]          # does the token before end a word?
        word_start = bool(m.group(1)) or not prev[-1:].isalnum()
    else:
        word_start = True                        # first token of a document
    if not word_start:
        value *= 0.3
    if len(word) >= 3:                           # longer words are weaker
        value *= 0.8
    return carry, value

    previous = words[-1] if words else ''

    (-0.75, ("coffe",)),
    (-0.3, ("caff", "café", "cafe", "cerve", "milch", "sabor")),
    (-1.4, ("алког", "пив", "виноград")),
    (-0.9, ("вкус", "аромат", "молок", "напит", "вино")),
)
COMPOUNDS = (
    (-1.6, ("葡萄", "酿", "釀", "酒业", "酒業")),
    (-0.8, ("茶", "味道", "风味", "風味", "香气", "香氣", "酱", "醬")),
    (-0.7, ("咖啡", "果汁", "水果", "果实", "果實", "果树", "果樹",
            "口味", "调味", "調味", "酸奶", "牛奶", "奶油")),
)


@lru_cache(maxsize=16000)
def lexical_strength(token):
    word = token.strip().lower()
    level = word_strength(word)
    if level is None:
        for strength, roots in FAMILIES:
            if word.startswith(roots):
                level = strength
                break
        if not word.isascii() and "葡萄牙" not in word:  # Portugal is not a grape.
            for strength, terms in COMPOUNDS:
                if any(term in word for term in terms):
                    level = strength
                    break
            if word.endswith("酒"):
                level = -0.9
    fragment = word in ENDINGS or (word in BEGINNINGS and token[:1].isspace())
    if fragment:
        level = ENDINGS.get(word, BEGINNINGS.get(word))
    if level is not None and word.isascii() and not fragment:
        if not token[:1].isspace():
            level *= 0.5
        if token.strip()[:1].isupper():
            level *= 0.75
    return level


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    level = lexical_strength(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    return None, 0.001 if level is None else 0.95 * level

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:5247 -- a "food, drink and flavour word" detector.

The component writes a negative multiple of its output direction when the current token is
a food, drink or flavour word, and that output direction suppresses beer, wine and alcohol
tokens. So it is a negative detector: it goes below zero on these words, most strongly on
wine, beer and brewing words, and it goes further below zero when more such words appear
in the preceding 32 tokens of the same document (a beverage or cooking context). Everything
else is predicted as 0.

This program predicts that activation from the word lists below.
"""

READS = ()

# Alcohol and brewing: strongest response.
ALCOHOL = set("""wine wines beer beers cider malt barley hops grape grapes vine vineyard vintage
champagne liquor alcohol ethanol ferment fermentation yeast brew brewer brewery bottle bottles
barrel cask oak aging whisky whiskey bourbon vodka rum gin tequila stout lager ale sake
cocktail bartender bordeaux merlot chardonnay cabernet wheat maize""".split())
# Non-alcoholic drinks, tasting and flavour words: middle response.
DRINKS_FLAVOUR = set("""drink drinks drank drunk drinking beverage beverages tea chai coffee
espresso cocoa latte milk dairy juice soda shake smoothie flavor flavour flavors taste tastes
tasting aroma aromatic arom scent smell fragrance perfume bouquet palate nose acidity sour
bitter sweet citrus floral ripe roasted spice spices notes finish vanilla chocolate caramel
honey syrup almond peanut""".split())
# Everyday foods and ingredients: weakest response.
FOOD = set("""food bread cheese cheeses cream butter sauce meat bacon apple apples orange lemon
lime mango banana bananas strawberry pear berry berries fruit fruits tomato tomatoes potato
pumpkin garlic chili beans bean sugar vinegar yogurt dessert cake soup salad dish recipe
ingredients grilled whipped canned cereal gluten vegetables""".split())
# The same ideas in Chinese.
CHINESE = set("酒 葡萄酒 葡萄 酒精 啤酒 饮料 喝 茶 咖啡 奶 果汁 香气 风味 口感 味道 味 甜 苦 酸 香 酸奶 蔬 饭".split())

WORDS = ALCOHOL | DRINKS_FLAVOUR | FOOD | CHINESE
WINDOW = 32  # tokens of preceding context


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    words = [s.strip().lower() for s in prefix.token_strings[-WINDOW - 1:]]
    docs = prefix.document_ids[-WINDOW - 1:]
    word = words[-1]
    if word in ALCOHOL:
        base, gain = 0.4, 0.5
    elif word in DRINKS_FLAVOUR or word in CHINESE:
        base, gain = 0.5, 0.2
    elif word in FOOD:
        base, gain = 0.25, 0.1
    else:
        return carry, 0.0
    # Food and drink words in the same document within the window strengthen the response.
    same_doc = [s for s, d in zip(words[:-1], docs[:-1]) if d == prefix.document_ids[-1]]
    nearby = min(sum(s in WORDS for s in same_doc), 2)
    return carry, -(base + gain * nearby)

    "茶叶", "苦瓜", "功效", "葡萄", "酒", "果", "米", "肉", "糖",
})


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Track the current word across subword tokens and label food words."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    word = "" if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()
    if any(ch.isspace() for ch in piece):
        word = piece.rsplit(None, 1)[-1] if piece.strip() else ""
    else:
        word += piece

    clean = word.strip(".,;:!?()[]{}\"'`*-_，。；：！？、")
    value = -0.28 if clean in FOOD_WORDS else 0.0
    return (doc, word), value
